video_title: The Deadline For Jalen Duren's Extension Is Days Away | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons are handling Jalen Duren's contract situation correctly
quotes.excerpt: I think the Pistons are handling the correct way to be completely honest with you.
quotes.quote: I think the Pistons are handling the correct way to be completely honest with you. I think they're rewarding him for a high level. I think they're trying to think for the future. They're going to give him $40 million a year to play basketball. They're trying to build a great team around you, but most importantly, a top-five player like Cade Cunningham. So, I think where they're trying to get to, especially as long as Cade is there, you want to try to win as much as possible.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren's poor playoff performance caused Pistons' contract hesitation
quotes.excerpt: What is giving the Pistons reason for pause is what happened in the playoffs.
quotes.quote: The facts are that if Jalen Duren had pulled his hamstring on the final day of the regular season, we wouldn't be having this conversation because the Pistons would have maxed him out. What is giving the Pistons reason for pause is what happened in the playoffs, which were a disaster for Jalen Duren. His numbers were basically cut in half. He was outplayed by other bigs, and he just didn't look like the franchise center that he looked like for most of the regular season.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons' roster moves have left them in a difficult position
quotes.excerpt: The Pistons are between a rock and a hard place too here.
quotes.quote: The Pistons are between a rock and a hard place too here because they can't just lose him for nothing. It's already been a weird off-season in Detroit. They trade away Isaiah Stewart. Say what you want about his anger issues out there on the floor, but he was a part of the fabric of that new old-school Detroit basketball. He was the Rick Mahorn of this era. They lose Tobias Harris, a productive guy for the two years. The Pistons' last two years have engineered one of the great revivals in the NBA. You're replacing him with John Collins, who's younger, I guess, but John Collins has been moved around a lot. He's seen a few franchises in the last couple of years.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Signing the qualifying offer would be a disaster for Detroit
quotes.excerpt: If he signs that qualifying offer, the Pistons are in a world of trouble.
quotes.quote: If he signs that qualifying offer, the Pistons are in a world of trouble because I don't think you can trade a guy after he signs the qualifying offer, at least there's a no-trade clause attached to a qualifying offer. And if that's the case, you lose Jalen Duren for little or nothing. You're kind of right back where you started with Cade Cunningham and a bunch of guys that are just okay. Jalen Duren has his flaws, but they need him there, or they need like Domantas Sabonis to replace him.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The financial risk of signing a qualifying offer
quotes.excerpt: You sign the qualifying offer, that's money you're never going to get back.
quotes.quote: You sign the qualifying offer, that's money you're never going to get back. You're never going to be able to recoup the difference between the one-year $10 million qualifying offer that you signed and the $50 million average salary that you would sign if you're Jalen Duren there. So it's a lot of money, and it's a big bet on yourself. That's why you never see guys do it. Remember when Kristaps Porzingis was leaving the Knicks and he was threatening to sign the qualifying offer when he got to Dallas? He didn't do that because guys don't do that. They don't leave that kind of money on the table.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Questioning the reports of a weight clause in Duren's contract
quotes.excerpt: Why are we even talking about a weight clause with Jalen Duren?
quotes.quote: What do you make also of the reports that the Pistons want to include a weight clause in this contract? Trajan Langdon, the GM there, came from New Orleans. There was a weight clause in Zion Williamson's contract for good reason. Whatever you want to say about Jalen Duren, he looks like he's carved out of a rock. Why are we even talking about a weight clause with Jalen Duren? Nobody in the NBA can really explain this to me. In fact, it's puzzled a lot of people that have seen the reports, and if they're true, just doesn't make a lot of sense.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Evan Mobley and Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: Who's better, Evan Mobley or Jalen Duren?
quotes.quote: Do you think who's better, Evan Mobley or Jalen Duren?

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Mobley is the better player

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Mobley's defensive impact and offensive development
quotes.excerpt: Evan Mobley is a former defensive player of the year.
quotes.quote: Evan Mobley is a former defensive player of the year, and while we are not in love with all of the offensive things that Evan Mobley does, he's still a developing offensive player.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner's assessment of Evan Mobley and Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: I'm grateful of what Evan Mobley brings to the game.
quotes.quote: I'm grateful of what Evan Mobley brings to the game, and I can confidently say like I don't expect whatever we're waiting for to show up. And I can say the same thing with Jalen Duren. Where they're at, I think they peaked. Besides like playing well playoff-wise, but even when you sit there like he's a ball-handler, he's making assists, like man, these strong ass passes. I don't want to see that shit. We're in trouble if Jalen Duren is handling the ball.
